Body: Requesting it too. I think this is an important feature that allows syncing the conversations of the same project across multiple devices.

Looks good, I had a PR that makes [following Symlinks opt-in](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/12992), which means you can just symlink the required folders in your project and start working
but this way also makes a lot of sense

> Thought I could share my bubblewrap setup that mimics OpenAI's codex sandbox:
> 
> # /home/<user>/.config/fish/functions/opencode.fish
> function opencode --wraps opencode --description "Run opencode in a strict Codex-style bwrap sandbox"
>     # 0. Resolve the real binary path to prevent symlink failures
>     set -l BIN_PATH (realpath (which opencode))
>     
>     if test -z "$BIN_PATH"
>         echo "Error: opencode binary not found in PATH."
>         return 1
>     end
> 
>     # Core bwrap arguments: read-only root, isolated namespaces, writable workspace
>     set -l BWRAP_ARGS \
>         --new-session \
>         --die-with-parent \
>         --unshare-user \
>         --unshare-pid \
>         --unshare-ipc \
>         --unshare-uts \
>         --cap-drop ALL \
>         --ro-bind / / \
>         --dev /dev \
>         --proc /proc \
>         --tmpfs /tmp \
>         --tmpfs /run \
>         --bind $PWD $PWD \
>         --chdir $PWD
> 
>     # 1. Protect .git (Mounts it as read-only so the agent can read history but not rewrite/corrupt it)
>     if test -d $PWD/.git
>         set -a BWRAP_ARGS --ro-bind $PWD/.git $PWD/.git
>     end
> 
>     # 2. Allow OpenCode to write to its own state/config directories if needed
>     # (Since the rest of ~ is read-only)
>     for state_dir in .config/opencode .local/share/opencode
>         if test -d $HOME/$state_dir
>             set -a BWRAP_ARGS --bind $HOME/$state_dir $HOME/$state_dir
>         end
>     end
> 
>     # Execute the actual opencode binary inside the sandbox
>     # 'command' ensures we bypass this function and call the real binary
>     command bwrap $BWRAP_ARGS -- $BIN_PATH $argv
> end
> 
> Results
> 
> Not 100% secure but gets the job done.

Thanks for the script , this didnt work as is in feodra,it broke network , I asked claude to fix it ,  I think the relvent part is this 
```
 # Restore DNS resolution (tmpfs /run hides this)
    if test -d /run/systemd/resolve
        set -a BWRAP_ARGS --ro-bind /run/systemd/resolve /run/systemd/resolve
    end
```
here is the minimal working script for me read only file system read only git
```fish
function opencodes --wraps opencode --description "Run opencode in a bwrap sandbox limiting writes to \$PWD"
    set -l BIN_PATH (realpath (which opencode))
    if test -z "$BIN_PATH"
        echo "Error: opencode binary not found in PATH."
        return 1
    end

    set -l BWRAP_ARGS \
        --die-with-parent \
        --ro-bind / / \
        --dev /dev \
        --proc /proc \
        --tmpfs /tmp \
        --bind $PWD $PWD \
        --chdir $PWD

    for state_dir in .config/opencode .local/share/opencode .local/state/opencode
        set -l full $HOME/$state_dir
        if test -d $full
            set -a BWRAP_ARGS --bind $full $full
        end
    end

    if test -d $PWD/.git
        set -a BWRAP_ARGS --ro-bind $PWD/.git $PWD/.git
    end

    command bwrap $BWRAP_ARGS -- $BIN_PATH $argv
end
```

Also there is no yolo mode , but this trick works https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8463#issuecomment-4050612237

Also this is useful so it doesn't oom `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G` (put it before bwrap)

even opencode serve works with this setup 

07/2026 update: there is a yolo mode now with --auto

I fixed this by deleting the opencode database and letting opencode recreate it
`rm ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`

```
~/.config/opencode via  v24.14.1
❯ rm ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db

~/.config/opencode via  v24.14.1
❯ opencode
Performing one time database migration, may take a few minutes...
■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 100% todos        2494/2494
■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 100% complete     2494/2494
Database migration complete.

```
FYI: I wrote a FastAPI proxy for this purpose.  It is independent of any coding agent.  We will be open-sourcing it soon.
